# OLYMPUS v0.0.6, "R says what it does": the build sheet

Written 2026-11-07 for the round's three implementers (actions, hair, menu) and the lead who integrates: the contract between roles building in parallel without talking. Where it is silent the docs decide (DESIGN.md and the user's rules, then TECH §1.3 on implementation, then the sections); my own choices are marked (my call); every disagreement settled here is in §8.

**The release.** A patch round (CLAUDE.md: "a batch of the user's patch requests"), not a ROADMAP scene: the user's two asks of 2026-11-06 after playing v0.0.4, logged in DESIGN.md as "the user on interactions" and "the user on hair", with the rules drawn from them. Verbatim:

> (1) "the shave+wash+water when pressing R at a basin without the tootip telling us what is going to happen is no good. First of all, implement ways of combining actions and quick action needs to be the most obvious. For the basin, first of all using the head shouldn't wash our hands either afterwards, then going to the basin, R should wash hands if hygiene is low enough, drink if we're thristy and shave if none of the above (use a priority thing and R is the most urgent), long pressing R should open the menu with all the possible interractions as single actions, with the ability to select several actions (not pre-combined actions like you do now that make lists hard to read), implement pixel art menu drop downs or checkboxes for multiselections"
>
> (2) "this haircut is not military acceptable, we should have to groom our hair the same way we will have to groom our beards and a soldier with half balding hair would 100% go fully shaved head for service."

**The user plays** Echo's barracks as before (v0.0.5's range untouched). From the urinal to a sink, the line says "R wash hands · 30 s" before R is pressed, and R does that and nothing else; at a sink with clean hands it says "R shave · 4 min, done 19:46" where stubble shows. R held opens a pixel-art menu of every single action there, each a checkbox, its time, or struck with why; three checked and Enter run one after another behind one splash, the total and the end shown first. Hair is a regulation cut that grows out over sols on the figure and the doll, the DI says "Haircut's due Thursday.", a shaved head is buzzed at a sink, the other cuts are the PX barber's.

**What the user must feel.** "Quick action needs to be the most obvious": one key, one action, named before you press. Lists that read: single actions, never bundles; a parameter (how long to sleep, which cut) a drop-down on its row, not eight rows. Grooming as a chore with a clock, like the beard.

**The user's rules hold over every section**: places authored, what happens in them procedural; every person generated; 16 px/m chibi; every picture and sound made by code; nothing pops in view (a cut changes only out of sight or behind a splash), no fast travel, graphics over words, no overlapping UI, AZERTY labels on physical codes (KeyR is R on both), every need runs through every gap.

**Rules of the round**: only your own files (§1); a change elsewhere is the smallest edit, said in your report; no commits, branches, tags, pushes, `release.sh` or `promote.sh`; never `.play/`, :8200, :8201, `../longhaul`, `../tradecraft` or `docs/research/`; browser work on your own port (planned: actions 8233, hair 8234, menu 8235, the integrator 8231 and 8232; **as run**, each role on the port its task gave it: actions 8231, menu 8232, hair 8233, the integrator 8236, the runtime and design reviews 8237 and 8239, none at the same time as another on one port), `OLYMPUS_TEST_PORT` for `tests/browser.mjs`, servers killed; CPU ceilings × `machine().k`, printed, and a quick suite over 60 s in the band said with its k; look at what you build (`node tools/shot.mjs`, 16 px/m). Docs and CHANGELOG.md are the lead's: return CHANGELOG bullets and doc items (file, section, exact change).

**Interfaces first.** Each role first writes §2's exports as stubs, then fills them; test against your own stub of a dependency until it is real, and say so. **Merge order**: actions (facts.js, the activities, the time domain, hand.js), hair (the body, the looks, the art), menu; `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs` after each. **A gunless, untouched game changes only where §3.3 says.**

## 2. Interfaces

JavaScript signatures; `state` the saved state, `bus` the core bus, `pid` a person id, times integer game ms; pure unless marked **w** (writes). Words in the sim are lower case; the HUD sets them in the pixel font's capitals.

Every other record as v0.0.5. Each new one has ≥ 4 log lines in TIME §8.8's voice. `stoppable` true everywhere; `resumable` false but the shower. A cut short `cut` or `clip` leaves the hair as it was (§8 item 9).

**Effects** (`partEnd` in `src/sim/time/activities.js`, each through BODY's doors, §2.2): `hands` whole → `groom(…, { hands: true })`; `face` whole → `groom(…, { face: true })`; `teeth`, `shave` as now; `clip` whole → `groom(…, { clip: true })`; `cut` whole → `cutHair(state, pid, { cut: args.cut })`; `go` (any share > 0) → `soil(…, { k: HANDS.HEAD, why: 'head' })`; `sit` → `soil(…, { k: HANDS.STALL, why: 'stall' })`; `eat` → `soil(…, { k: HANDS.FOOD, why: 'food' })`; the shower's `water` (f > 0) → `wash()`, which now also cleans the hands (the hair role's door). **The range** (taken `shooting.js endSub`): a handling sub-step ended (every sub but `aim`, `hold`, `fire`, `wait`, `finger`, `show`, `observe` and `stance:*`; as built after §9, also not a magazine's `reach`, `lookMag`, `stowMag`, `dumpMag` or `dropMag`: `shooting.js` `CLEAN_SUBS`) → `soil(…, { k: HANDS.RIFLE_SUB, why: 'rifle' })`; a `stance:kneel` or `stance:prone` ended outdoors → `soil(…, { k: HANDS.REGOLITH, why: 'regolith' })`. No roll reads the hands (§8 item 4).

**Where** (`idsAt`): `wash` (a sink) → `['wash-hands', 'teeth', 'shave', 'clip', 'wash-face', 'drink']`, filtered by who you are (no `shave` row for a woman, no `clip` row but for a shaved head); `haircut` (the barber's pole) → `['haircut']`; the rest as v0.0.5.

```js
ROWS = { wash: ['wash-hands', 'teeth', 'shave', 'clip', 'wash-face', 'drink'], … }   // the menu's order and a chain's (my call: the order one does them in)
PRIORITY = { wash: [['wash-hands', 'hands'], ['drink', 'thirst'], ['shave', 'stubble'], ['clip', 'haircut']], toilet: [['bowel', 'bowel'], ['urinate', 'bladder']],
             sleep: [['dress', 'drill'], ['standfast', 'drill'], ['sleep', 'night'], ['nap', 'day']], … }        // the tests named here, coded in hand.js
BARBER_H = [10, 20]          // the barber's hours, Melas time (PLACES §4.13's PX, 10:00 to 20:00)
WASH_HANDS_MS 30_000; CLIP_MIN 10; HAIRCUT_MIN 12
```

**The priority tests** (hand.js; the first that holds is R's quick action; none holding, the first unstruck row in `ROWS` order; every row struck, R goes on down its order: a door, the resume, the wait; *as built after the fixer's §10 item 1*: at a spot with a `PRIORITY`, none holding, R goes on to the door or the wait, the first unstruck row being R's only where a spot has no `PRIORITY`):

|---|---|
| `hands` | the hands' band is `dirty` or past (`HANDS.WASH_AT_I` 2: dirt ≥ 40) |
| `thirst` | thirst's band is `thirsty` or past (i ≥ 1: a 1% deficit) |

| `haircut` | a shaved head whose `hairOf().band` is `due` or past |
| `bowel` | the bowel at `could-go` or past (v0.0.5's rule) |
| `bladder` | the bladder over `URINATE_MIN_ML` 50 |
| `drill`, `night`, `day` | v0.0.5's rack rules: a drill open (dress if not in utilities, else stand fast), 20:00 to 05:30, else |

**Struck reasons** (`offOf(state, id, spot, args) → null | words`, shown with the row and never done): shave "clean-shaven" (under 12 h), clip "buzzed today" (under 1 sol since the cut), urinate "nothing to give" (≤ 50 mL), dress "already in PT kit" / "already in utilities", a sleep or nap choice "reveille comes first" (it would run past reveille, or reveille is under `SLEEP_MIN_MS` 20 minutes away), haircut "the barber opens at 10:00" / "the barber shut at 20:00", any row "taken" (someone within `FIXTURE_FREE_M` 0.5 m). **As built**, two more (the actions role's): "reveille is over 12 h off" ("until reveille" where its plan, capped at `SLEEP_MAX_MS`, would end before reveille) and "not your cut" (a haircut cut outside `cutsFor`); and two from the fixer's §10 item 4: "fresh from the barber" (a haircut at `hairOf`'s step 0) and "freshly buzzed" (the clippers at step 0 past a sol). `startActivity` refuses every struck action with its words. A late row is not struck: it carries `late` and goes through the late card.

**R** (`src/sim/places/hand.js`; its order unchanged: rise, the spot's action, a door, the resume, the wait; null while stop motion or a range session is open, as v0.0.5):

**The chain** (new `src/sim/time/chain.js`; TIME §8.1, §5.3; §8 items 10 to 15):

```js
planChain(state, { spotId, steps: [{ id, args }] }) → { ok, why, steps: [{ id, args, label, fromMs, toMs, durMs, off }], durMs, endMs, label, kind, late }
  // each step planned from the end of the one before (planOf gains { fromMs, wearing }: the time and the outfit the steps before leave), every
  // step's end but the last on its first whole second (as planOf's parts); kind = kindFor(total); late = lateCheck on the whole; label
  // 'brush teeth, shave, wash face · 7 min, done 19:53'; a step struck or not at this spot: ok false, why its off
startChain(state, bus, ctx, { spotId, steps, late = null, force = null }) → { ok, why }      // w
  // TIME §5.3's checks once (standing, at the spot, free, not busy); late 'fit' keeps the leading whole steps that end by fitMs (none: refused),
  // 'accepted' runs it all; writes time.chain, starts step 0 as startActivity would (no lead) and begins ONE skip over the chain's total
  // (ctx.sim.beginSkip, kind by the total, vignette the first non-null of the steps', mask step 0's); posts 'chain-next' at step 0's toMs
onChainNext(state, bus, ev)        // w; the event 'chain-next' { prio: 5, src: 'time:chain', payload: { i } } at step i's toMs, in every engine:
  // finishActivity(step i) (its own outcome, log line and 'activity' end), then step i + 1 begun at the same ms (doing written, its parts'
  // events posted, the next 'chain-next' unless it is the last), skip.activity and skip.mask set to it; a step refused at its start
  // (taken, not at the spot) ends the chain there ('chain' { phase: 'end', by: 'refused' })
chainStop(state, bus)              // w; Backspace ('skip:stop' while time.chain runs): stopAt = the running step's toMs, skip.toMs = stopAt,
                                   // 'chain' { phase: 'stop', toMs }; the step runs to its end, the rest dropped
chainNow(state, ms) → null | { spotId, steps: [{ id, label, fromMs, toMs, done }], i, n, stopAt }      // the splash's view
```

The last step ends with the skip (`finishSkip` closes it, then the chain: `'chain' { phase: 'end' }`, `time.chain` deleted, `outcome.chain` in `skip-end`). An interrupt the running step's mask lets through cuts that step at its fraction (a shower left resumable) and drops the rest (`by: 'interrupt'`, `dropped`). `liveStep` leaves a chained step's end to `chain-next`. A chain of one is never sent: the UI sends the single (`activity`, with its lead). A chain never leads (a sleep in one lies you in the berth behind the splash, v0.0.4's way). **Inputs**: `{ act: 'chain', args: { spotId, steps: [{ id, args }], late?, force? } }` (time domain's action; the menu's and the late card's); the single as v0.0.5 (`{ act: 'activity', args: { id, spotId, args, lead: true } }`, a door's and the wait's `{ act: 'hand', args: { want } }`).

**The instinct** (`instinct/base.js`, `instinct.js`): `stubble`'s act becomes `activity:shave`; new **`hands`** (note, before `stubble`): the hands at `dirty` or past and a sink at hand (T: `activity:wash-hands`; "Wash your hands." ≥ 4 phrasings), or within `HANDS_NAG_MS` 120,000 of the head or a stall wherever you are, no act ("The basins. Wash your hands."); quiet in a drill, on the range, asleep or busy. `instinct.js` merges the hair role's `GROOM_RULES` by tone after `BASE_RULES`, before `RANGE_RULES`.

### 2.2 hair (BODY §6; VIEWS §3, §4.2; PEOPLE §6.2, §11.10; the user's ask (2)), and the hands ledger's body

**The hands** (`body.hands`, a ledger in the stepper beside grime; §8 item 3):

```js
HANDS = { RATE_K: 1.0,        // × grime's hourly rate (BODY §6: 1.2 awake, 0.5 asleep, +1.5 outdoors, +1 over MET 5), closed form, linear
          HEAD: 40, STALL: 60, FOOD: 10, RIFLE_SUB: 1.5, REGOLITH: 15, WASH_AT_I: 2 }      // my calls; to 100 at most
HANDS_BANDS = [{ id: 'clean', tone: 'fine', fill: 0, words: 'Clean hands.' }, { id: 'used', tone: 'fine', dirt: 20, words: 'Your hands could do with a wash.' },
               { id: 'dirty', tone: 'note', dirt: 40, words: 'Dirty hands.' }, { id: 'grimy', tone: 'warn', dirt: 70, words: 'Grimy hands.' }]
soil(state, pid, { k, why }, ms, bus)              // w, BODY's door: dirt + k (≤ 100), why; 'body-event' { kind: 'soil', amount: k, why }
groom(state, pid, { teeth, shave, face, hands, clip }, ms, bus)   // w; hands: dirt 0, why null; clip: hair.h 0; amount's bits gain hands 8, clip 16
wash(state, pid, { waterMin, cold }, ms, bus)      // w; as v0.0.5, and the hands to 0
```

`why` is the last soiling ('head', 'stall', 'food', 'rifle', 'regolith', or null from the slow rate alone); the words name it ("Dirty hands, since the head.", "Gun oil and carbon on your hands.", "Regolith ground into your palms."). `stagesOf` gains `hands`; `cuesOf` gains `handsK` (dirt / 100) and `handsWhy`; `wordsOf` gains the `hands` row. `LEDGERS` gains `hands` (no interrupt). The squad's hands read the template's (clean) until PEOPLE's needs at 0.0.9: nothing reads them this round. The template's dirt is the reference sol's at reveille (about 5: washed at 21:45, a night at 0.5 an hour); `sol.js`'s heads soil and its basins wash (`groom: { hands: true, … }`), so `startBody` gives the same hands lived or skipped.

```js
         braid: { sex: 'f', word: 'braid pinned up', sidesMm: null, topMm: 300, dueSols: 42 } }
HAIR_STYLES = { m: [['highTight', 30], ['lowReg', 35], ['medReg', 25], ['shaved', 10]], f: [['bun', 55], ['short', 30], ['braid', 15]] }   // weights my calls
THIN_P = [[18, 0.10], [25, 0.16], [30, 0.30], [40, 0.50]]     // a man's chance his hair is thinning, by age (after Norwood 1975: type III or more in about a sixth of men under 30, half by their forties)
LEGACY_CUTS = { m: { crew: 'lowReg', short: 'medReg', bald: 'shaved' }, f: {} }      // the upgrade's map
KIT.styles = Object.keys(CUTS)                                 // 'bald' and 'crew' gone from the data and the art
```

**Thinning means a shaved head**: a man is thinning when `hashFloat('hairline', seed, lookSeed) < THIN_P(age at the roster's reference time)` (cosmetic, by hash: no stream moves; my call), and his only cut is `shaved` (`look.hair.thin: true`, saved, read by the barber's drop-down). The roster's squad rule (VIEWS §3.9) runs over the seven cuts (men and women now share none), a thinning man's options `shaved` only; its codes and `cellsFit` follow; clashes still counted.

**The hair** (`body.hair = { h }`, hours since the last cut, grown every second in the stepper as `stubbleH` is: `h += dtH`, rounded to 1e-12 at each cell's end; §8 item 19):

```js
HAIR = { MM_DAY: 0.40, STEP_K: [0.3, 0.7, 1.0] }   // scalp hair 0.40 mm a day (Loussouarn et al. 2005: about 0.26 to 0.41 mm a day by ethnic group; "about a centimetre a month"); 0.411 mm a sol
HAIR_BANDS = [{ id: 'fresh', tone: 'fine', words: 'Fresh from the barber.' }, { id: 'growing', tone: 'fine', k: 0.3, words: 'Growing out.' },
              { id: 'due', tone: 'note', k: 0.7, words: 'Haircut due {day}.' }, { id: 'over', tone: 'warn', k: 1.0, words: 'Out of regulation.' }]
hairOf(state, pid, ms) → { cut, word, sex, thin, h, sols, mm: { sides, top }, step: 0..3, band: { id, i, tone, words }, dueMs, dueDay, regulation }   // src/sim/body/hair.js: THE helper
  // the player (a body with atMs): the ledger; anyone else: the squad's closed form; no body (the sandbox): step 0. step and band by sols / dueSols
  // against STEP_K; mm = the cut's + MM_DAY × h / 24; dueDay = WEEKDAYS[weekdayOfSol(the sol the cut reaches dueSols)]; regulation = band.i < 3
squadHairH(seed, pid, cut, ms, lonEDeg) → h        // the closed form: a cycle of 0.7, 0.8 or 0.9 of the cut's dueSols by hash('barber', seed, pid) (men 7, 8 or 9 sols: in
                                                     // regulation always), phased by hash, each cut at 12:00 local of its sol (PEOPLE §6.2's barber need, "sols since haircut / 7")
cutsFor(person) → [cut]                            // a thinning man ['shaved']; else his sex's
setCut(state, pid, cut, ms, bus) → bool            // w person.look.hair = { ...old, style: cut } (a new object, so the view's memo sees a new look); 'look' fact
cutHair(state, pid, { cut }, ms, bus)               // w, BODY's door: hair.h 0, setCut where it changed; 'body-event' { kind: 'haircut', cut }
withLedgers(body, { handsDirt, hairH, … })          // the scenes' and tests' names
```

**On the figure** (`figure.js`, `place.js`, the art): `lookFor(look, outfit, indoors, step)` puts `hair.step` in the wear() spec (the memo keyed by it); the player's step is `hairOf()`'s; everyone else's is `actor.hair`, which `whereIs` gives and `setPose` writes **only where the player cannot see** (`lookAt`'s rule, so a squadmate's cut never happens in view; an actor without it draws the closed form's step until then). The art draws every cut at its four steps in every view and every frame that shows the head, the sleeper included (`bedding.js`), each step at least 2 px apart from the next at 16 px/m (the sides from skin, to a shadow, to dark, to the hair's colour; the top a pixel taller at step 3; the bun and braid alike but for stray pixels at step 3); `compose.js`'s `bald` cases become `shaved` (the wet sheen on the scalp kept); the default cut is `lowReg`. **The doll** draws the same cuts and steps, and the hands by `handsK` and `handsWhy` (grey for the slow rate and the head, black-grey gun oil, rust regolith; the band's share of the hand's pixels). `view.js`: `PART_FRAME` gains `hands: 'basin'`, `clip: 'shave'` (the hand at the head; no new pose), and the sleeper's spec passes the step.

**The barber** (§8 item 20): a fixture `f:melas:px:barber`, kind `barberPole` (planned: `w` 0.3, `d` 0.15, `h` 2.2, no block, `mount: 'wall'`, `uses: ['haircut']`, one spot `{ n: 1, dx: 0, dz: 0.5, use: 'haircut', face: 'up' }`, on the PX's north face 2 to 3 m east of its door (292, 430), facing north; **as built** (the hair role's, because this camera looks north and the PX's 4 m roof hid anything on its north face): **0.36 × 0.36 × 2.2 m on its own stand, blocking, `sightH` 0, at (294.5, 425.6) facing north**, 2.5 m east of the door and 4.4 m out from the wall, its one spot 0.65 m beside it at **(293.85, 425.6)**, facing it, so the pole never stands between the player and the camera; two makes, `pole` and `lit`), its spot reachable on the ground's grid; drawn by code (a red, white and blue spiral in a glass tube, a cap, readable at 16 px/m). R there: "haircut (high and tight) · 12 min, done 14:52"; you go in (the figure hidden, `inside`), behind a splash with no vignette, and come out fresh-cut. The PX's interior and its three chairs wait for PLACES §4.13's building.

**The instinct's `haircut` rule** (new `instinct/groom.js`, `GROOM_RULES`): `due` a note, "Haircut's due Thursday." (the day from `hairOf().dueDay`; ≥ 4 phrasings), `over` a warning ("That hair is out of regulation. The barber, today."); by day (05:00 to 21:50), quiet in a drill, on the range, busy or lying; T: `activity:clip` at a sink with a shaved head, `activity:haircut` at the barber's pole, else none (the words say where: "The barber's at the PX, 10:00 to 20:00." or "Clippers. Head A has mirrors.").

**A new join arrives fresh-cut**: the template's `hair.h` is 24 (cut the day before shipping), so New career's player starts at step 0, `fresh`. **The squad keeps its hair in regulation** by `squadHairH`, never seen being cut. **PEOPLE §11.10's rule, written for the inspections to come**: a cut is in regulation while `hairOf().regulation` (under its `dueSols`: men 10, women's short 21, bun and braid 42; my call on the women's).

### 2.3 menu (VIEWS §7, §8, §10.1, §11; the user's "pixel art menu drop downs or checkboxes")

**R's plate.** R's words always show before R is pressed: `offerWords(offer, { armed })` → `{ key, text: 'wash hands · 30 s', more }`, drawn by `hud/instinct.js` as a plate in the pixel kit at the right of INSTINCT, **on every line, urgent ones included** (§8 item 7), the line shortened before the plate; `more` (handOffer's `rows` > 1) a small "…" mark on the plate's corner. *As built*: the integrator counted the rows other than R's wait (`rows` > 2, or other choices), and the fixer's §10 item 2 made the mark "HOLD ▸" in brass at the plate's right, with the struck note before the keycap. R tapped does the plate's action (v0.0.5's `wantOf`, the wait asked twice); **R held** (`TAP_MS` 220, keys.js, unchanged) opens the menu wherever `handMenu` has a row.

**The kit** (`src/ui/kit/`, pure but `mount.js`; Pixmaps `{ w, h, data: Uint32Array }` in ImageData's order, as `plaquePixels`):

```js
KIT = { face, hi, lo, ink, text, dim, strike, cursor, late }      // the plaque's 'way' plate and the step panel's tones
textPixels(text, { colour }) → pm          // src/art/font.js's 3 × 5 capitals and plaque.js's marks (· × ( ) = ?); the 5 × 7 of src/art/kit/type.js for a title
platePixels({ w, h, kind = 'way' }) → pm   // the plaque's enamel: ink outline, lit top, shaded foot, nicked corners
checkboxPixels({ checked, off, focus }) → pm        // 7 × 7: ink frame, lit face, a 5-pixel tick; struck: a grey cross, never a tick
dropPixels({ words, open, focus, w, items, pick }) → pm      // a box with its ▾; open, its items listed below it, the picked lit
rowPixels({ n, checked, words, timeText, off, late, focus, drop }) → pm    // the digit, the box, the words, the time right-aligned; struck: the words through, the reason after
createList({ rows, multi = true }) → list   // { rows, cursor, checked: Set(keys), picks: { key: i }, open: key | null }
list.key(code, { shift }) → { changed, sound: null | 'move' | 'check' | 'uncheck' | 'confirm' | 'close', act: null | 'do' | 'close' }
list.point(x, y, kind: 'move' | 'down' | 'up') → same                            // the mouse, in kit pixels
list.chosen() → [{ id, args }]              // the checked in row order, else the cursor's row; struck rows are never chosen
list.layout() → { w, h, rects: { rows, boxes, drops, doIt } }
mountPixels(canvas, pm, { scale }) ; hitOf(rects, x, y)        // whole CSS pixels a kit pixel: round(3 × --ui), my call
```

**The menu card** (`src/ui/cards/actions.js`, R held; it pauses, as every card does, so the times hold): one canvas of pixel art on VIEWS §8.1's dark glass. Its title (`handMenu().title`) on a plate; up to ten rows, "1 ☐ WASH HANDS · 30 S", "4 ☒ BUZZ YOUR HEAD · 10 MIN (BUZZED TODAY)"; a row with choices carries its drop-down ("SLEEP [UNTIL REVEILLE ▾] · 8 H 15 MIN"); the cursor row lit; the foot "TOTAL 7 MIN · DONE 19:53" from `planChain` of the checked (or of the cursor's row), amber with the late's words when late; a "DO IT" plate; the keys line "1-0 · ↑↓ · SPACE CHECK · ENTER DO · ESC" (*as built after the fixer's §10 item 3*: "1-0 CHECK · Z S ↑↓ · ENTER DO · ESC", with " · Q D CHOICE" where a row has a choice). **Keys**, read by the card itself by `KeyboardEvent.code` while it is open (main.js's onAction leaves them to it): Digit and Numpad 1 to 0 move the cursor to the row (*as built after the fixer's §10 item 3*: they also check it); ArrowUp and ArrowDown (and KeyW, KeyS: Z and S) move; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (KeyA, KeyD: Q and D) change the cursor row's choice; Space checks or unchecks (a struck row: its reason flashed, nothing checked); Enter and NumpadEnter do the checked, else the cursor's row; Escape or KeyR close. **The mouse**: hover moves the cursor, a click on a box checks it, on a drop-down opens it (a click on an item picks it), on DO IT is Enter, outside the card closes it. **What it sends** (the card closes first): one row, the single (`activity` with its lead, a door's or the wait's `hand`); two or more, `{ act: 'chain', args: { spotId, steps } }`; a late plan, the late card first (`cards/late.js` as v0.0.5, its answer added to the same input). **Sounds by code** (`src/data/sounds.js`, `uiShot`): `uiMove` (a 12 ms tick), `uiCheck` and `uiUncheck` (a latch click, the second lower), `uiConfirm` (two rising notes), `uiClose`; and `clippers` (a 120 Hz hum and its harmonics through a 2 kHz band, a loop) in `world.js` while a `clip` part runs, the tap's loop while `hands` runs (my calls, unscored, VIEWS §11.5).

**The splash** (`hud/splash.js`): a chain's outcome strip lists each step's line in order (from `skip-end`'s `outcome.chain`), the dropped ones named; the ticker's keycap reads "Backspace: stop after this step" while a chain runs; on `chain` `{ phase: 'stop' }` the shown clock decelerates to the new end as an interrupt's does (TIME §6.5, `DECEL_S` 0.35 s). **The sheet** (`cards/sheet.js`): a Hands row (`wordsOf`) and a Haircut row (`hairOf`: "High and tight · growing out", "Haircut due Thursday."); "Head wet." for a `shaved` cut. **main.js**: `BODY` gains `hairOf`; the sheet's and the inventory's dolls get `lookFor(p.look, outfit, indoors, hairOf(…).step)`; the choices card's code goes. **The handle**: `menu()` (handMenu), `hands()`, `hair()`.

### 3.1 The fields

- **`time.chain`** (TIME's key, TECH §6.1): `{ spotId, fromMs, toMs, i, stopAt, late?, steps: [{ id, args, toMs, done?: { fraction, by, line } }] }`, null outside; no id (one at a time, nothing for the ids walk). `time.doing.chain` the running step's index. **`body.hands`** `{ dirt, why }` and **`body.hair`** `{ h }`: new groups in `GROUPS` and both templates (`hands: { dirt: 5, why: null }`, `hair: { h: 24 }`), saved as deltas (TECH §6.6), dirt to 1e-9 and h to 1e-12 at each cell's end. **`look.hair`** `{ style, color, thin? }`, `style` a `CUTS` key. **`actor.hair`** 0 to 3, a squadmate's drawn step (people's, written only unseen).

### 3.2 The upgrade (a v0.0.5 save loads)

- **The cuts: written.** People's upgrade `people:cuts` (flag `mig:people-cuts`) maps every look's style by `LEGACY_CUTS` (crew → lowReg, a man's short → medReg, bald → shaved; women's as they are) and draws no thinning: v0.0.4's bald men are the shaved ones. The squad rule still holds (the map is one to one within a sex).
- **The body: nothing written, the template fills.** A record without `hands` or `hair` reads the template's (`dirt` 5, `h` 24) at its own `atMs`, and the stepper carries them from there (TECH §6.6, rule 2): an old save's player reads a day-old cut. Neither the load nor the first tick writes them; the first sync stores them once they differ.
- **Activities: kept.** The `legacy` `basin` record and sleep's `turn-in` part finish a save made mid-activity as v0.0.5 would; nothing offers them. **Actors**: none has `hair` until placed unseen; the figure reads the closed form meanwhile. **The chain**: an old save has none.
- **Proof**: two saves made with v0.0.5's own code (a scratch worktree of the tag, removed after): `tests/saves/v0.0.5-barracks-basin.json.gz` (19:31, the bundle's shave part running behind its splash) and `v0.0.5-barracks-turnin.json.gz` (21:56, R at the rack in utilities, sleep's turn-in running). v0.0.3 and v0.0.4 saves pass their own upgrades, then `people:cuts`.

### 3.3 What a gunless, untouched game changes

Only these, each on purpose: **the roster** (`GOLDEN_ROSTER`: the cuts' ids and weights, thinning by hash, the squad rule over seven cuts); **the player's body** (the `hands` and `hair` groups in its deltas: the reference sol's heads and basins, the slow rate, the hair's growth); **actors** (the squad's `hair` step); **the sandbox** (`GOLDEN_SANDBOX`: its look's `crew` becomes `lowReg`, nothing else); **places** (`GROUND_AREA`: the barber's pole). Unmoved: `MELAS_PLAN`, `ECHO_1`, `ECHO_2`, `TEST_AREA`, `KD_RANGE`, `RANGE_PIECES` and every grid. Nothing that moves, sleeps, eats or drills changes its time or place: the integrator diffs a v0.0.5 and a v0.0.6 barracks run of 6,000 ticks (seed 48213, 21:00, no input) and finds only the paths above. test-handling's digests move by the hands alone.

## 5. Tests

Names are sentences in the files; here the suite, what it **prints** and what it **holds**. Numbers six spaces in; assertions carry their evidence; a test pinning the user's ask names their words and the date ("the user, 2026-11-06: …"); CPU ceilings × `machine().k`, printed.

### 5.1 actions

- **`time-actions`** (quick, new). **Prints** every spot's rows with their words, times and struck reasons (a sink for a man at 14 h of stubble, a woman, a shaved head at 8 sols; a urinal empty and full; a toilet stall; your rack by night, by day and in a drill; your locker; a tap; a machine; the barber's pole at 09:00 and 14:00; a door; nothing at hand), and R's quick action over a grid at a sink (hands clean or dirty × thirsty or not × stubble or not × shaved due or not). **Holds** the user's priority exactly ("R should wash hands if hygiene is low enough, drink if we're thristy and shave if none of the above", 2026-11-06); no row is two actions (every row one activity of one part, but the shower's); "the head shouldn't wash our hands": after the head the hands are `dirty`; R's label names what it does and its time ("wash hands · 30 s", "shave · 4 min, done …"); a struck row is refused by `startActivity` with its reason.
- **`time-chain`** (quick, new). **Prints** a chain of brush teeth, shave and wash face: its plan (7 min, the end), each step's boundaries and line, the body before and after; the same chain forced live, ff and outcome side by side; Backspace at 1, 3 and 6 minutes (where it ends, what is dropped); a reveille-cut chain; a late chain fitted. **Holds** one skip and one `skip-start`, three `activity` ends in order, `outcome.chain` of three; the three engines' bodies within `time-parity`'s tolerances and the same boundaries to the ms; Backspace ends at the running step's end, never mid-step; an interrupt cuts the running step and drops the rest; **saves mid-chain carry on byte for byte** (a save at every outcome step and every 20th ff tick, reloaded, the same final digest).
- **`moment-basin`** (heavy, new; the integrator's acceptance in node, §6 item 3), its bot `basinRoutine` in `tests/bots/routine.mjs`.
- **`time-activities`**, **`time-review`**, **`instinct`** (the scripted morning: the head, then "Wash your hands." at the sink, T, then the shave by T), **`game-upgrade`** (the two v0.0.5 saves: load, `people:cuts` applied, the legacy activity finishing as v0.0.5 did, 3,000 ticks with no error, a save after carried on byte for byte), **`game-domains`** (every fact of §2.4 registered and emitted) updated; **`moment-shower`**, **`moment-night`**, **`scene-handling`** and the range bot, **`game-walk`**, **`time-parity`**, **`time-placement`** green, their numbers read.

### 5.2 hair

- **`body-hands`** (quick, new). **Prints** the hands through the reference sol (each head, meal and basin), through test-handling's course, and the slow rate's times to each band awake, asleep and outdoors. **Holds** the events' amounts; a basin and a shower clean them; a split anywhere equals one call (as `body-skip`); lived and skipped equal; the words name the cause.
- **`body-hair`** (quick, new). **Prints** each cut's lengths and steps at 0, 3, 7, 10 and 14 sols; the squad's cycles and steps over 30 sols (never `over`); the due day said. **Holds** 0.40 mm a day ±0.01; `h` after an 8-hour skip equals 8 hours lived; `clip` and `cutHair` reset `h`; a thinning man is only offered `shaved`; New career's player starts `fresh`.
- **`figures-hair`** (heavy, new). **Prints** each cut × step × view composed at 16 px/m and the doll's, with the pixels changed between consecutive steps; shots to `.run/figures-hair/`. **Holds** no `bald` and no `crew` in the art or the data; each step ≥ 2 px from the next on the head (but bun and braid, which change only at step 3); a cut never drawn over a cover.
- **`instinct-groom`** (quick, new): "Haircut's due Thursday." on the right day, quiet at night, in a drill and on the range; T buzzes at a sink, cuts at the pole.

### 5.3 menu

- **`ui-kit`** (quick, new). **Prints** each piece's pixels as text (a checkbox checked, unchecked, struck and focused; a drop-down closed and open; a struck row; a plate). **Holds** the list's keys by code (Digit1 to Digit0 and Numpad, the arrows and KeyW, KeyS, KeyA, KeyD, Space, Enter, Escape, KeyR) and the pointer give the changes and sounds listed; a struck row never checks; `chosen()` keeps row order.

## 8. Resolutions, and doc changes for the lead

Implementation by TECH §1.3, the rest by DESIGN.md and the user's rules; each (my call) unless a source is named.

1. **A patch round, three roles**: actions (the sim of R, the singles, the chain), hair (the body's two ledgers, the cuts, the art, the barber), menu (the plate, the kit, the card).
2. **The basin's bundle splits into six single actions** (wash hands, brush teeth, shave, buzz your head, wash face, drink), and **the head no longer washes hands** (the user, 2026-11-06). TIME §8.2's "hands included" goes from `urinate`.
3. **The hands ledger lives in BODY's files, built by the hair role** to this sheet's rules, so the body has one owner this round; the actions role owns what soils and washes it and who reads it (R, the DI, the menu).
4. **The hands are a ledger, 0 to 100, beside grime**: a linear closed form at grime's rate plus events (the head +40, a stall +60, a bar +10, the rifle +1.5 a handling sub-step, regolith +15), washed to 0 at a basin or a shower; four bands; no roll reads them this round; the squad's read clean until 0.0.9.
5. **R's quick action is a priority per spot, as data** (`PRIORITY`), the first test that holds, else the first unstruck row; at a sink the user's order, then a shaved head's buzz; teeth and the face are never urgent.
6. **Sleep and the nap no longer change your clothes**: the turn-in was a bundle; you sleep in what you wear, R at the rack still offers sleep first, and the menu chains dress then sleep. `moment-night` (already in PT kit) is unchanged. R's sleep now always begins lying, so the page's R lies you down in sight first in utilities too (v0.0.5's lead, about 4.8 s from a lower berth): the `splash-sleep` bench (R at 21:57 in utilities) keeps its keys and its wait grows by the lie-down (the actions role, `src/data/bench.js` taken for that number only), so it still times the whole night's splash.
7. **R's words show on every line, urgent ones included**, as a plate at the right of INSTINCT, against SKILLS §14.1's "except on an urgent line" (the user's ask: R must say what it will do before it is pressed).
8. **", done HH:MM" only from 45 s**: a lived action ends in front of you ("wash hands · 30 s").
9. **A cut or buzz cut short changes nothing**; the barber's is not resumable.
10. **A chain is one skip** over its total, its steps on whole seconds, each ended by a `chain-next` event in every engine, so lived and skipped meet the same boundaries; the running step's mask is the skip's.
11. **A chain runs in the menu's order**, which is the order one does them in, not the order checked.
12. **Backspace in a chain stops at the running step's end**; an interrupt cuts the running step and drops the rest (a shower left resumable).
13. **A chain is checked late as a whole**; "fit it in" keeps the leading whole steps that fit; steps are never shortened inside a chain.
14. **One fixture a chain**; a chain never leads (a sleep in one lies you down behind the splash); a chain of one is sent as the single.
15. **The menu pauses** (VIEWS §8.1: every card does), so its total and end hold; it reads its own keys by code while open; R or Esc closes it.
16. **The cuts are CAREER §2's seven**, with lengths and weights my calls, ids `highTight`, `lowReg`, `medReg`, `shaved`, `bun`, `short`, `braid`; men and women share none, which loosens VIEWS §3.9's squad rule (16 men's pairs where 12 were).
17. **Thinning means `shaved`, drawn by hash** against `THIN_P` (after Norwood 1975), stored as `look.hair.thin`; all shaved heads are drawn alike, never a horseshoe.
18. **Old saves map their cuts** (crew → lowReg, a man's short → medReg, bald → shaved) and draw no thinning: v0.0.4's bald men are the shaved.
19. **Hair is hours since the cut** (`body.hair.h`), grown as stubble is; lengths, steps and bands come from it and the cut, by one helper, `hairOf`, at 0.40 mm a day (Loussouarn et al. 2005).
20. **The barber is a pole at the PX's north door**: R there, 12 minutes behind a splash with the figure inside, 10:00 to 20:00; the interior waits for its building. *As built*: on its own stand 4.4 m out from the wall at (294.5, 425.6), not on the wall (the camera looks north and the 4 m roof hid it), 0.36 × 0.36 × 2.2 m, blocking, its spot at (293.85, 425.6) facing it; makes `pole` and `lit`.
21. **The cuts get a sample** (`samples/cuts/`: each cut at its four steps at 16 px/m and on the doll) for the user to star and score; the game draws them as built until scored (CLAUDE.md: the look is chosen from scored samples).
22. **Women's cuts keep their own clock**: short within 21 sols, bun and braid within 42; men's within 10 (PEOPLE §11.10 said 10 for all).
23. **The squad's barber is a closed form**, a cycle of 0.7 to 0.9 of the cut's due (men 7 to 9 sols) by hash, cut at noon of its sol, the drawn step written only out of the player's sight.
24. **The body's new groups fill from the template, nothing written on load** (`hands.dirt` 5, `hair.h` 24): an old save's player reads a day-old cut; the cuts' map is the one written upgrade.
25. **The legacy `basin` and `turn-in` stay in the table, never offered**, so a v0.0.5 save made mid-activity finishes as it would have.
26. **The clippers reuse the shave's frame**; no new pose.

**Doc changes for the lead**: CHANGELOG.md (the roles' bullets), README's "Where it stands", PLAYTESTS.md (Claude's play of §6 items 6 and 7); DESIGN.md's log (a 2026-11-07 entry for items 2 to 26, each my call, overrulable; the two 2026-11-06 entries marked built in v0.0.6); TIME §8.1 (the chain: 10 to 14), §8.2 (the singles' rows; `urinate` without hands; `haircut`), §8.4 (6), §6.4 and §6.5 (12), §9.5 (13); VIEWS §3.9 and §3.4 (16, 17, the steps), §4.2 (the doll's hands and hair), §7.1 and §7.4 (7), §8.2 (the Hands and Haircut rows), §8.10 (choice cards: the R menu, its kit, 15), §10.1 (R tapped and held), §11.3 (the menu's sounds, the clippers); SKILLS §14.1 (7), §14.4 (the `hands` and `haircut` rules); BODY §2.5 (`hands`, `hair`, 24), §6 (4, 19, the cuts' table); PEOPLE §5.5 and §6.2 (23), §11.10 (22); CAREER §2 (16, 17); PLACES §1.5 (`barberPole`), §4.13 (20); TECH §6.1 (`time.chain`), §6.6 (the groups); CONTRACTS §9 (`body.hands`, `body.hair`, `time.chain`, `actor.hair`, `look.hair.thin`), §11 (§2.4), §13 (`hairOf`, `handMenu`, `planChain` as shared helpers).

## 9. Arms, the user's 2026-11-07 asks

Written by the arms role, on the tree as the integrator left it (§1 to §8's interactions and hair joined and green). The user's report on test-handling (v0.0.5, seed 452580432), verbatim, and the rules DESIGN.md's log draws from it (2026-11-07):

> "Gun system is very close, slight bug (I think ?) in the demo scenario we don't get enough mags for the whole exercise, I shoot two prone, two kneeling and when I have to shoot standing, I don't have any mags left. There should be some way to select which mag we put in as well because we may have different types of rounds in inventory, putting magazine in should be a "Reach for magazine" (or equivalent) and when we have the mag we reached for, we see if it has ammo in and which kind before we decide to either put it away again, drop it or put it in. Because I can't shoot standing I can't finish the exercise and rate it but let's say that it's 98% there and shippable as is, very good job. One minor nitpick is that on the gun drawing, the magazines are very long, if they could be a bit slicker it would be nice"

**The cause, from their save.** In the prone string they fired four, changed magazines by the singles (Magazine to the dump pouch, Magazine in) and fired six more; the kneeling string took the third magazine; at "Standing. RELOAD." the three magazines lay empty on the firing point, and the tower waited for Condition 1 (`stand1`) for ever. The singles' change drew no fault: only the RELOAD macro was checked against the tower (`aheadOf`). Loaded in this build, their save plays to the end card and the score card: "Clear at 09:02 · 70 of 75 · 7 V · 1 string not fired · 2 faults".

**Files.** `src/sim/arms/` calibres.js, kit.js, firearms.js, drills.js, shooting.js, shot.js (the shot's load), look.js (the fire's load and lane); `src/sim/scenarios/handling.js`; `src/data/courses.js`; `src/core/debug.js` (the setup `mixed`); `src/art/weaponcard.js`, `src/art/figures/templates.js` (the rifle's magazine), `compose.js` (the loose magazine); `src/render/range-items.js`, `range.js`; `src/ui/hud/steps.js`, `src/ui/cards/inventory.js`, `src/ui/cards/tests.js` (sceneSaid), `src/ui/audio/range.js` (a tracer lands dull), `src/ui/style.css` (the marked row), `src/main.js` (two fault words, the I card's ground reach, a magazine look's toast); tests below; `tests/saves/v0.0.5-handling-nomags.json.gz`. **Smallest edits in others' files**: `src/main.js` three lines (the menu role's), `src/ui/style.css` two rules (the menu role's), `src/ui/cards/tests.js` one line, `src/art/figures/compose.js` the loose magazine's two lines (the hair role's file this round).

**Resolutions** (each my call unless a source is named):

27. **A scene never dead-ends** (the user's rule): the coach's check. While the tower waits on a command that wants rounds (`NEEDS_ROUNDS`: LOAD's `magIn`, MAKE READY's `cond1`, a string's `emptyLocked`, the RELOADs' `kneel1` and `stand1`), once `checkMs` 3 s of it is lived, the shooter still and the rifle free of a stoppage (a double's loose round is being cleared, not missing), the coach counts what the shooter has (`roundsLeft`: the chamber's live round, the magazine in, the hand's, the pouches', those at the feet); none, and he says so in his voice ("Nothing left to load. You sit this one out, on safe.") and the session is dry (`R.dry`). The RO's readiness then takes "no rounds, on safe, in the stance" for every string left, each sat out (`R.sat`), scored as not fired (the coach: "That string goes down as not fired."; the end card: "1 string not fired"); the course runs on to UNLOAD, SHOW CLEAR.
28. **The line moves on**: a command not answered after `moveOnMs` 60 s of lived time (the nudge at 30 s before it) is passed over, a `slow` fault in the coach's words ("The tower will not wait for you. Keep up."), the next command posted after the usual gap; at UNLOAD, SHOW CLEAR the coach takes the rifle (`coachClears`: the magazine to a pouch, the chamber and a double's loose round thrown, the bolt home, cocked, safe, the port shut, slung front), shows it clear himself and says "Clear.". Lived time only: a player choosing in stop motion is never hurried. An idle shooter from the brief reaches the end card at +9.4 minutes with nine `slow` faults.
29. **One magazine a string** (the user's rule): the magazine in the rifle at a string's commence fire, or the first seated during it, is the string's (`R.strMag`); seating another before the tower's RELOAD is a fault `onemag` each time, the coach's "One magazine a string. You reload on the tower's word." the first (`magSeated`, called at every seat in stop motion). A RELOAD macro chosen while the line is hot is no longer the `ahead` warning too (one act, one fault). The panel marks every step that would seat another magazine (`warn: 'one magazine a string'`, amber, not struck: `oneMagWarn`).
30. **Reach for a magazine is magIn's first half** (the user's ask): `reach` (0.6 s, no roll, rushable) and `seat` (0.8 s, DC 9, the old roll whole), both × `LONG_K`, so at Weapon handling 10 they make 691 + 921 = 1,612 ms against magIn's 1,611 (each rounded to its millisecond; within 1 ms at every tier) and LOAD, MAKE READY and the RELOADs live the ticks they lived (2,450 ms for LOAD): the range bot's whole course is unchanged to the tick and the point. A reach rolls nothing (WEAPONS §3.3: "reaching for one is part of the step's time"), so the dice stream is unchanged too. magIn stays, the two in one, for v0.0.5's saves made mid-LOAD and for REMEDIAL ACTION, whose stripped magazine is brought back from the hand that racked in the reach's time (its 6.05 s stands).
31. **The places a hand reaches** are named by key (`kit.js pouchesOf`): `p1`, `p2` ("chest pouch 1", "chest pouch 2", the chest's magazine pouches in reach order), `dump` ("the dump pouch"), `ground` (a magazine at your feet, within `FEET_M` 1.2 m: a pickup, `PICKUP_S` 1.0 s, no `LONG_K`, a magazine off regolith taking `PICKUP_DUST` +0.1, WEAPONS §5.5). An action id carries its place after `@` (`reach@p1`, `stowMag@p2`; `actionKey`, `actionPlace`, `actionOf`). A reach into a named pouch takes the magazine at its front; one put back goes in behind it, so reaching again brings the next (the player chooses: the drills' rule would hand back a known ball for ever over a tracer not yet seen).
32. **In the hand you learn what it holds**: its weight at once, the truth's band of its capacity (`feelOf`: none; a few to a quarter, 1 to 7 of 30; about half to 0.6, 8 to 18; nearly full, 19 to 29; full), no roll; written to the magazine's belief (`feel`) when its count is not known, and a band that contradicts the count believed (by more than ±1 when that count is a guess) makes the count unknown and halts a drill, the rest queued ("From chest pouch 1. It feels empty. You thought 5 rounds."). **Look at it** (`lookMag`, 0.6 s, DC 4, dark +4, careful, routine for the trained): the witness holes give the count as a magazine check's window does (exact to 20, ±1 above), the feed lips the top round's kind ("5 rounds, tracer on top: a red tip."; the coach's orange dummy when it is the top round); a failure learns nothing and says so.
33. **The steps for a magazine in hand** (the user's "either put it away again, drop it or put it in"): Magazine in (`seat`), Look at it, Put it back (`stowMag@pN`, 1.0 s, DC 5, each chest pouch with room), Dump it (`dumpMag`, 0.7 s, DC 4), Drop it (`dropMag`, 0.3 s, no roll; on the firing point's paving a drop's wear, on regolith none). While one is in the hand no reach is offered; a fumble that bites drops it. The panel's reach rows say what each would bring as believed: "Reach: chest pouch 1 (5 ball, 1 of 2)", "Reach: at your feet (empty, 1 of 3)".
34. **The drills reach by rule** (`rankOf`): a magazine believed empty last of all; then the kind the gun is meant to fire (`meantLoad`: the session's load, ball on the range) believed, a kind not known, another kind; the fullest believed within it; ties in reach order; never the ground. With a magazine already in the hand, a drill seats it and reaches for nothing. (Found playing setup `mixed` by the keys: "RELOAD, keep the empty" had reached for the empty it had just dumped, believed ball, over full magazines of a kind not known; the empty-last key fixes it and a test pins it.) A drill's reach says nothing in J and raises no toast unless its weight surprised it (its seat's "A magazine in: 5 rounds." says the rest); a single reach says what the hand felt.
35. **Kinds of rounds** (the user's "different types of rounds"): calibres.js gives each live load a word and a tip (`LIVE_LOADS['6.5x40r']`: ball, its bare copper; tracer, a red tip, my call), one kind a magazine (mixed loads, a tracer every fifth, wait for the belts). A magazine's belief gains `kind`, the gun's `load` (the kind of the magazine in it), moving with the magazine as its count does; a round carries its kind into the chamber (`gun.load`, saved only when not ball), out of the muzzle (`pull()`'s and the shot's `load`) and out of the port (`'tracer'`, a live tracer thrown). The issue's magazines are told their kind with their count (`newMag toldKind`).
36. **Setup `mixed`** (`?play=test-handling&setup=mixed`): the `range-mixed` kit, the three magazines of ball and a fourth of five tracer, second in chest pouch 2, the counts told and the kinds not ("One of your magazines is tracer: the course is ball."); the tracer is its own ammunition issue line (`R.issueIds`), a tracer fired counted there. The course stays all ball (familiarisation fire); LOAD by rule never takes the tracer once a ball is known.
37. **A tracer drawn**: lying, brass with a red tip (`brassPixels`, `SHAPES.tracer`); in the weapon card's window, the top round's nose a red pixel; on the I card's icon the same. **The shot's look**: the trace proper lights at `traceFromM` 30 m, beyond the 25 m card, so by day what shows is the igniter's dim ember, a dotted dull-red streak (`EMBER` 0x8a3a2e, every other pixel) 3 m behind the round as it flies at 790 m/s from the drawn muzzle to the card's centre, 32 ms at 25 m: one or two frames at 60 Hz, no bright trace (`TRACE` only past 30 m).
38. **The magazines drawn shorter and slimmer** (the user's nitpick): on the weapon card (144 px/m, the 0.92 m rifle 132 px) the HAD-30's 0.21 m is `MAG_HIDDEN_M` 0.045 m up in the well and `MAG_SHOWN_M` 0.165 m below it, 24 px and a 2-px baseplate, `MAG_W_PX` 7 px wide (4.9 cm), curving 8 px forward; v0.0.5 drew the whole 0.21 m below the well, 30 px and a 3-px plate, 9 px wide, curving 14 (its pixels with shadow and ink 416 in a 27 × 38 box, now 280 in 19 × 31). On the figure's rifle (16 reference pixels for the drawn 1.0 m) the magazine is one reference pixel wide, stepping forward as it goes down, two below the receiver: 2 cells at 16 px/m (12.5 cm below the well, 6 cm front to back) and 7 at 24 px/m (a 2-wide band three rows deep), against v0.0.5's 4 and 12; the doll's rifle takes the same shape; the loose magazine in the hand three quarters of `magM` long, a pixel thick at 16 px/m, two at 24.
39. **The weapon card shows the magazine in hand as believed**: under the handguard in a hand, its window to its believed count with the top round's tip, "?" when nothing is known, and under it its count ("5", "≈5"), its weight's band ("A FEW") or "?", "TR" in red when believed tracer; the empty well then says MAG OUT by itself. The card's line adds "HAND 5 TR"; the rifle's own count is followed by "TR" when the magazine in is believed tracer. `beliefOf` gains `magLoad` and `hand` (believed fields only: `{ fam, n, approx, load, feel, cap }`).
40. **The I card** names each pouch ("Chest pouch 1", "Chest pouch 2", "The dump pouch"), each magazine with its believed count and kind ("5 in it, ball", "5 in it, kind not seen", "a few by its weight"), and two tiles more when they hold anything: in your hand, at your feet (the reach a pickup's and a seat's).
